subject.title: fix: allow trusted host-read html after outbound staging

question: Should OpenClaw accept content-bound SQLite provenance as the trust signal for generated HTML after outbound staging?
rationale: The patch appears to fix the message-loss regression without trusting the whole outbound directory, but it still changes the local HTML host-read security boundary and stored state lifecycle, which needs maintainer intent rather than automated approval.

options.title: Accept provenance-gated outbound trust
options.body: Approve the sha256+size SQLite marker lifecycle and merge after the branch is rebased cleanly.

options.title: Require tighter lifecycle bounds first
options.body: Ask for additional cleanup bounds such as TTL/chunked pruning or upgrade proof before accepting the boundary expansion.

options.title: Reject outbound HTML host-read trust
options.body: Keep staged HTML blocked and pursue a different product path such as PDF conversion or hosted report delivery.

recommendation.title: Accept provenance-gated outbound trust
recommendation.body: Approve the sha256+size SQLite marker lifecycle and merge after the branch is rebased cleanly.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete authored the trusted generated HTML host-read seam in PR 87982 and is the strongest routed owner for accepting or rejecting the boundary extension.
